description: The reporter registry (spec section 10.1): the reporters official for a court's decisions (official, spec section 5.9), the reporters that are editions of one report (editions, section 7.1), and the dates of decision each volume of the Supreme Court's reporters prints (supreme_court_volumes, section 4). Reporters are named by their slug (section 5.6), which from 0.7.0 is the slug of the abbreviation registry/reporter-variants.json gives.

ny.source: New York Reports: State Reporter created by the Judiciary Act of 1847 (L 1847, ch 280), https://history.nycourts.gov/biography/george-comstock; N.Y. Judiciary Law §§ 431 and 433-a (L 1938, ch 494; L 1950, ch 820) and CPLR 5529(e), text at https://www.nycourts.gov/reporter/Regulations.shtml: causes determined in the Court of Appeals are published in bound volumes entitled "New York Reports"

nyalbanycityct.source: L 1892, ch 598 ("An act to provide for reporting the decisions of the inferior courts of record in the state of New York", approved by the Governor May 14, 1892), § 1: the Governor appoints a miscellaneous reporter "who shall hold office for five years from the first day of July, eighteen hundred and ninety-two" to report opinions "in causes decided in any court of record of this state, other than the general terms of the supreme court and in the court of appeals"; § 7: "This act shall take effect September one, eighteen hundred and ninety-two" (Laws of 1892, pp. 1144-1145, https://books.google.com/books?id=p_rWqKbZ7sEC&pg=PA1144); 1 Misc. title page: "In pursuance of Laws of 1892, chapter 598", earliest decisions July 1892 (https://static.case.law/misc/1.pdf); Judiciary Law (L 1909, ch 35) § 447: "The said reports shall be known as the 'Miscellaneous Reports'"; continued by N.Y. Judiciary Law §§ 431 and 433-a (L 1938, ch 494; L 1950, ch 820) and CPLR 5529(e), text at https://www.nycourts.gov/reporter/Regulations.shtml: causes in any other court are published in the Miscellaneous Reportss

supreme_court_volumes.source: Computed from CAP's case metadata (static.case.law mirror, as of 2026-09-30): for each volume of the United States Reports from 5 that CAP holds, the dates of the decisions it prints; for every other volume, the dates of the Supreme Court decisions that CAP lists with a citation to it, grouped where they are more than 550 days apart, keeping the group of 5% or more of them that fits the volumes before and after it, and leaving out a volume out of sequence with the one before it; a volume's first date is then no later than the last date of the volume numbered before it, since a volume opens with orders entered between terms, which CAP's dates rarely show. A person has not checked it (codexpublicus/exemplar#50).
